Yes. The subtext feels natural and enriches the story rather than forced. Q’s toes pressing against his instep reveal strain beneath his composed manner, while Lydia’s renewed enthusiasm exposes how his kindness also lets him postpone an uncomfortable refusal. The narrator’s decision not to announce himself suggests envy, shame, and an uneasy awareness of the power that overheard information provides.

The pool setting strengthens these tensions: an ordinary family outing becomes the backdrop for professional disappointment and a daughter’s hurt. The damp, permanently marked book quietly echoes the narrator’s altered understanding of Q without imposing a single interpretation.
